The Cataclysm pin 09a75ac is newer than the 6c506a pin used by the earlier engine-absorption review; that earlier review covered conditions, effects, magic and persistence, not this appendix's proficiency/job path. repositories.title: CoffeeMUD

source.cache_limit: Pinned partial mirror; this review inspected the README, root license and notice, and one teacher behavior, not the full MUD, content set, or all notices for bundled dependencies.

purpose_and_rights.observed: README identifies CoffeeMud as an MUD and directs operators to separate LICENSE and NOTICE files. LICENSE is Apache-2.0. NOTICE names CoffeeMud contributors and third-party components including JZLIB, Rhino, CodeMirror and NicEdit.
purpose_and_rights.reuse_boundary: No code, prose, assets, or third-party dependencies were copied. Any later code reuse must retain applicable Apache notices and review each dependency's separate terms; inspiration alone needs no copied-file attribution.

repositories.reviewed_mechanism: MOBTeacher is a configurable MOB behavior. It can seed abilities/classes/expertise; when a visible human student speaks a teach/gain request, it parses one requested ability or expertise, checks student qualification/known state and routes teaching through the engine's postTeach service. It has explicit rejection/report paths for invisible parties and the broad 'ALL' request. This is a dialogue affordance over CoffeeMud's own class/ability mapper, not a stand-alone student-teacher economy. The behavior also has broad setup modes, including periodic expertise provisioning, which should not be mistaken for a bounded per-lesson model.
repositories.fit: Selective pattern only. YAIR already has explicit knowledge, acquisition, practice, actual power/source effects, native skill consumers, NPC schedules and directed memory. The useful narrow seam is letting an eligible instructor expose a finite known method after observed evidence and a direct request. No whole CoffeeMud behavior or dependency is warranted.
repositories.code_backed_no_fit: The source depends directly on CoffeeMud MOB, char-class, ability-mapper, command, and expertise services; those types cannot serve as a drop-in YAIR runtime. Its ability-to-student postTeach call also does not prove what costs or saved state a future YAIR lesson should use.
repositories.partial_coverage: One MOB teaching behavior and repository-level rights files only.
repositories.notice_and_content_limits: The NOTICE lists bundled third-party projects with separate licenses. Repository Apache-2.0 status does not by itself clear game world text, art, or each bundled library for YAIR.

repositories.title: OpenNefia current C# source

source.cache_limit: Pinned partial mirror; inspected project README/license, TrainerSystem, and VanillaAISystem excerpts only.

purpose_and_rights.observed: README describes a work-in-progress, moddable engine reimplementation of Elona requiring .NET 8. LICENSE is MIT and names Noa and Ruin0x11.
purpose_and_rights.reuse_boundary: No code or assets were copied. The code license does not establish permission to copy Elona's original game content; any future content reuse needs a separate provenance review.

repositories.reviewed_mechanism: TrainerSystem exposes a default learnable-skill list plus per-map trainer additions, computes training cost from the learner's current skill level, scales new-skill cost by a saved total-skills-learned counter, and computes potential gain from current potential. The interface does not make these costs payments to the trainer or consume trainer-owned inventory/time. Separately, VanillaAISystem documents that the default entity system can be replaced per NPC, handles NPC turn events and evaluates help, item verbs, combat, search, and calm actions in an ordered sequence; calm behavior is explicitly not yet implemented in this pin.
repositories.fit: Selective authoring pattern. A trainer's finite per-location allow-list and visible formula are useful for original YAIR profession content. Its global saved count is a tuning choice, not a required shared economy or a reason to add a new trainer engine. The AI replaceability seam is architecturally interesting but YAIR already supplies typed controllers that choose legal command/response paths.
repositories.code_backed_no_fit: EntityUid, EntitySystem, map components, turn events, .NET service dependencies and the tile-oriented tactical AI do not match YAIR's synchronous browser-game executor. The TrainerSystem has no teacher resource reservation or directed lesson memory in the inspected subsystem.
repositories.partial_coverage: Trainer calculations/allow-list and selected default AI action order only; no full entity-component or Elona content review.
repositories.maintenance_and_fallback: If later content needs a trainer roster, define it in existing simulation content and use current command eligibility and acquisition effects. Drop the roster data without migrating runtime state if that content is removed; preserve already learned powers and knowledge. Adding a saved per-teacher counter would need a migration decision, and is not justified by this code alone.

repositories.title: OpenNefia archived Lua prototype

source.cache_limit: Pinned partial mirror; inspected archived README/license, Lua trainer dialog and the compact NpcMemory API only.

purpose_and_rights.reuse_boundary: No Lua source, game content or assets were copied. Original Elona provenance is separately relevant to content.

The trainer interaction is superseded by the current C# source review; the definition-level count memory is too coarse to substitute for YAIR's per-person knowledge and directed relationships.
repositories.partial_coverage: One trainer dialogue and one small memory module; no prototype-wide comparison.
repositories.maintenance_and_fallback: Do not make new YAIR code depend on this retired Lua API. If a simple confirm-and-pay dialogue is later needed, express it using the current native interaction and simulation command contracts; remove the authored trainer option without deleting existing actor-specific memory.

repositories.title: Cataclysm: Dark Days Ahead

source.cache_limit: Pinned partial mirror; this lane inspected proficiency definitions/runtime persistence, a consumer surface, and faction mission definition loading. Earlier audit evidence at 6c506a remains authoritative for its named EOC/condition/save paths only.

purpose_and_rights.observed: README identifies a turn-based survival game. LICENSE.txt declares CC BY-SA 3.0 for Cataclysm and lists separate licenses for fonts and other components.
purpose_and_rights.reuse_boundary: Pattern-only recommendation. Do not copy code, JSON, dialogue, assets, or documentation into YAIR from this source. Any later content or code reuse needs a fresh rights and attribution review for the exact files and distribution.

repositories.reviewed_mechanism: Proficiency definitions carry learnability, category, practice timing/penalty/bonus, prerequisites, teachability, and bonuses. Character practice advances saved time-based learning with focus adjustment; a completed method emits an event and is separately queryable as known or in-progress. proficiencies_offered_to exposes only teachable proficiencies known by the teacher and missing from the student. A native window makes learning time, prerequisite links and progress inspectable. In the pinned lockpick activity, missing lockpicking proficiency multiplies action duration, and completing the activity advances the relevant proficiency practice. Faction mission definitions load authored skill, difficulty/risk/activity, time, positions, item alternatives, effects and footer fields. These are separate mechanisms, not proof of a single universal profession simulation.
repositories.fit: Strong independent design pattern for distinguishing learned method, active practice, prerequisites, eligible teachers and a real downstream use from a label-only skill. YAIR already has simulation power mastery, acquired sources, explicit observation/knowledge, paid practice jobs, real material effects and native skill/function consumers. The gap is selective content joining an actual NPC as an authorized teacher to one method and presenting prerequisites/time transparently, not a second skill ledger.
repositories.current_pin_refresh: New pin 09a75ac was checked for the added proficiency and faction mission scope. Prior selected pin 6c506a in the engine-absorption appendix established other condition/effect/magic mechanics. This lane does not claim that old source paths are unchanged or that the new pin refreshes every old finding.
repositories.partial_coverage: Proficiency definition/practice/offer/display path and faction mission definition loader only; not all crafting consumers, NPC dialogues, assets, or save serialization.
repositories.maintenance_and_fallback: Use existing YAIR power/mastery, knowledge and native ability consumers; if no qualifying concrete world lesson is selected, retain the current explicit player practice and acquisition routes. Do not port their broad proficiency vocabulary or faction data. New durable teaching records, if truly needed, require an explicit compatibility/migration design.

repositories.title: DFHack

source.cache_limit: Pinned partial mirror; reviewed README, license documentation, workflow documentation/implementation entry, and autolabor documentation/implementation entry only. It does not have a persistent rule that maintains min/max output stock or a general labor auction; neither is needed for the current first realm.

source.cache_limit: Pinned partial mirror; inspected README, BSD license, and the core Script timer/persistence module only.

findings.title: Teach a finite known method through an eligible person
findings.upstream_observation: CoffeeMUD resolves a human learner's explicit requested skill against qualification and known state before calling its teaching service (MOBTeacher.java 337-458, 517-558). Current OpenNefia keeps a default and per-map allow-list and calculates distinct costs from current skill level and saved total lessons learned (TrainerSystem.cs 26-75). Its archived Lua trainer separately selects a skill, shows a price, checks funds before confirmation, and invokes either training or learning (trainer.lua 32-99). New-pin CDDA offers only teacher-known methods marked teachable and absent from the learner, while practice state has its own path (character_proficiency.cpp 71-135).
findings.inference_and_novelty: YAIR already implements this core pattern for its current skill slice: timber method is observed from the named craftsman, instruction is separately acquired through a finite co-located timed lesson, actual teacher focus and a material are spent, directed knowledge records the teacher, practice uses a separate timed job, and mastery changes actual kit output. Lio's lesson similarly charges the target's own stamina. These repositories confirm choices already in code and do not justify another teacher system. A finite authored teacher offer-list abstraction might help future content, but the four selected skills bind their teachers directly and no shared roster contract is currently missing. The player's native money fee remains a sink, with no instructor income implied.
findings.original_yair_example: The existing Village example already joins two actual logs, one player-side coin sink, one craftsman focus, co-location, a dry workbench, a three-minute lesson, directed observation/instruction, later separate practice and a native kit-output use. This connected implementation is present in src/skill_expansion_content.js and src/simulation_content.js; its current gameplay gate remains implemented-unverified. It is not a new lesson proposal.

That is an authoring abstraction question, not a missing playable teacher behavior for the current four skills. NPC resources are actor-owned; native money applies only to the player, so payer cost does not credit an instructor.

findings.route: No new feature is recommended from this finding. Preserve current named-teacher bindings. If several future worlds establish a shared need for data-driven teacher rosters, consider a small authoring-only helper over existing rules and effects. Reuse no source code or runtime dependency.

findings.title: Keep method understanding, practice, and functional benefit separate
findings.upstream_observation: CDDA proficiency definitions expose prerequisites, teachability, training duration, focus handling, and typed bonuses, while Character::practice_proficiency advances a separate saved learning state and emits a completion event. Its UI shows learning time, progress, prerequisite and downstream links. OpenNefia's trainer methods distinguish a known-skill increase from potential on a learned-but-untrained skill. CoffeeMUD maps teaching to an actual ability/expertise learner state after qualification rather than presenting a teacher label alone.
findings.inference_and_novelty: A useful method can have evidence/understanding, acquisition, gradual practice, and a bounded functional consumer as separate facts. Current YAIR already has those owners for its selected four skills, including native XP and competence, so a parallel proficiency graph would duplicate progression. Remaining value is content authorship that uses real prerequisites and downstream outcomes, not copying the subsystem.
findings.original_yair_example: The current workbench path is a connected YAIR example: a commission transfers two actual logs and records that the craftsman has the material; his scheduled controller reserves the workbench and consumes his owned wood to produce the actual survey kit; collection records interpreted knowledge; the player can separately study the method and use measured packing; timber judgment's chosen consumer changes actual kit output. A future teacher offer can point to these existing phases, with the existing discovery/practice/consumer chain. It must not grant stock, mastery or XP merely because a UI row was rendered.

current_yair_owner_and_missing_consumer.missing: A generic content schema for declaring prerequisite graphs/skill offer links may help only if several actual realm methods need it. The present YAIR skill catalog already has authored observation/acquisition/practice/use bindings; no missing global method engine is established.

findings.route: Keep current typed contracts and author a data-only connection for each selected method. No external dependency. Later widen catalog schema only when more than one independent world needs a genuinely common new field.

findings.title: Bound stock-aware work and profession decisions to an authored local policy
findings.upstream_observation: DFHack workflow protects repeat jobs and suspends/resumes production around per-item target/gap rules; its docs distinguish this convenience from more expressive native workorders. Autolabor presents three explicit assignment modes, ranks eligible workers by skill and policy, keeps upper/lower worker bounds, saves mode, and warns the legacy approach may disable modern work detail behavior or produce poor assignments. CDDA faction_mission's definition loader exposes an authored set of skill/risk/time/position/item alternatives/effects for specific mission types. Evennia's ScriptBase persists timed repeats as part of its always-running multiplayer server.
findings.inference_and_novelty: These are three different layers: production stock maintenance, workforce routing, and authored mission data. YAIR has finite one-off site phases, exact inventory/job effects and repeat programs, but no min/max stock-band consumer and no general labor-auction consumer. It should add only an explicitly selected local stock policy; automatic whole-cast job assignment would be a new system and is not implied by current foundations.
findings.original_yair_example: Second connected proposal: an optional Village workshop policy can keep a small band of Prepared survey kits by asking the named craftsman to repeat one eligible, already-authored recipe only below its lower target and pause above its upper target. A policy preview names exact wood/tool costs, existing workbench reservation and teacher/worker eligibility; each paid job still uses current schedule, material ownership, claims and real output publication. The notebook can report observed shortage or blocked inputs with who noticed them. Disablement stops starting work, leaves a paid job's frozen due time and materials intact, and records no free stock. This would add bounded stock-band selection to the existing finite program/site-project paths, not generic worker reassignment. It remains a proposal, not playable behavior.

current_yair_owner_and_missing_consumer.missing: No simulation command currently wakes from a saved min/max inventory target, has stock gap/hysteresis, or explains one persistent stock policy's status. Existing automatable programs have a finite count and pause when the next costs/access are unavailable; site projects are one-shot phases.

findings.route: Prototype one opt-in local authored policy in the existing simulation scheduler only if a selected playable campaign needs it. Do not use DFHack or Evennia as dependencies. A local proposal should read exact current stock and work through existing previews/claims/jobs; do not add general labor autonomy.

Preserve current authoring fallback: one-shot project phases or finite programs, with visible pause reason. Remove a policy by stopping future starts while retaining already-paid job settlement.

findings.title: Choose the existing simulation seam over an imported actor or timer framework
findings.upstream_observation: Current OpenNefia documents replacing its VanillaAIComponent-backed entity system by another entity system responding to NPC turn events. Evennia Scripts provide persistent server objects and Twisted real-time timers. DFHack plugins operate against Dwarf Fortress's process-owned structs and native job state.
findings.inference_and_novelty: A seam is useful when it keeps a real authority boundary visible: OpenNefia's event extension point, Evennia's durable timer object, and DFHack's native state coupling each belong to their host architecture. YAIR's typed simulation controllers, scheduler, owned effects, existing source/body models and durable publication already provide corresponding seams. Importing any full framework would add a second actor/timer/save authority and complicate single-realm compatibility without supplying a currently missing consumer.
findings.original_yair_example: The current craftsman controller selects among actual command previews by authored priority, while each job deducts its authored costs from the specified owner, consumes real logs, reserves the shared bench, completes on the existing clock, writes attributed results and publishes through the one save boundary. A new behavior should register a legal command or narrowly extend that controller, not independently tick an NPC or mutate native inventory.
